title: Dedicated reservation auction and fairness: backfill, eviction, and burst controls (PRD)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: As Dedicated customers scale, static reserved pools lead to inefficient utilization during predictable slack and unpredictable churn. Current soft-burst and preemption rules are coarse-grained: they either allow bursts that unfairly starve long-running tenants or preempt aggressively and cause visible SLA regressions. We need a PRD for a reservation auction and fairness layer that enables: (1) auctioned short-term reservation windows during low utilization, (2) intelligent backfill that respects tenant priority and evict budgets, and (3) clear eviction and burst policies surfaced in the Console and API. This will reduce wasted reserved capacity, improve fairness across tenants, and provide deterministic fallback behavior under contention.
background: Existing related PRDs focus on reservation windows, QoS shaping, and soft eviction. However we lack a transparent mechanism that: a) lets tenants bid (internal credit model) for short-term burst capacity, b) caps eviction impact via budgets and grace periods, and c) ties auctions to autoscale pre-warms and kernel scheduling signals. Operators currently respond to unfair burst usage with manual throttles and tickets. This PRD defines a systematic, observable approach that integrates with billing and the Console for tenant transparency.
goals:
1) Define an auction-based short-term reservation system (ephemeral reservations) that runs during sustained idle periods and reacts within 30s to utilization changes.
2) Design fair backfill when reserved pools are underutilized: prefer short-lived auctions and low-cost tenants while preserving minimum alloc guarantees.
3) Specify eviction budgets and graduated preemption rules that limit per-tenant evictions to a defined percentage of in-flight requests and provide automatic recovery paths.
4) Surface auction outcomes, eviction events, and credits in Redwood Console and billing reports.
5) Provide clear, testable acceptance criteria and rollout gating to avoid regressions for hosted API customers on mixed infra nodes.
non_goals: We are not building a full marketplace with external trading or pricing discovery. This PRD does not redesign per-token pricing or resolve enterprise legal billing terms. It does not change existing SLA commitments for dedicated reserved instances beyond defined safe rollout limits.
requirements: Functional: Implement ephemeral reservation auctions that run every 60s and allocate short-term capacity windows of configurable length (default 10m).
Functional: Auction engine must accept tenant bids in credits and output ranked allocations with a fairness score combining historical utilization, priority, and bid amount.

Functional: Backfill policy should allow low-latency backfill where the runtime can pre-warm model weights and KV caches and still meet tenant p95 latency SLOs in 95% of cases measured over 1h windows.
Functional: Eviction budget per tenant: configurable as percent of concurrent connections and max evictions per hour; default budget 5% of concurrent token streams and 3 evictions/hour.
Functional: Soft-eviction path must attempt a graceful degrade (reduce batch size, switch to quantized model variant, or route to a lower-tier capacity pool) before hard-killing requests.
Observability: Emit structured audit events for every auction, allocation, backfill decision, and eviction with tenant id, reason, and pre/post capacity state.
Console: Add a Reservations dashboard showing auction history, credits spent, backfill usage, and eviction incidents with links to logs and traces.
API: Expose a read-only endpoint for tenants to view upcoming ephemeral reservations and their remaining credit balance.
Safety: Provide a global kill-switch to disable auctions and backfill per-region with zero-downtime fallback to current reservation behavior.

Performance: No increase in P99 latency for non-affected tenants beyond 1% during steady-state; during auction processing transient spikes are acceptable but must be documented and limited to under 5s for control-plane ops.
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests for auction logic covering tie-breaking, priority weighting, and credit accounting (100% pass in CI).
End-to-end load test showing: effective utilization improvement of reserved pools by at least 12% in representative workload replay while maintaining tenant p95 latency SLOs for 99% of tenants.
Eviction budget enforcement validated: eviction events do not exceed configured budget in a 72-hour stress window in staging.
Console features implemented: reservations timeline, credit ledger, and per-tenant eviction history available and linked to traces; QA-approved by UX with no major issues.
Safety: Global auction off switch works and fallback behavior reverts to pre-existing reservation semantics with no lost allocations within 5m of toggle in staging.
Security: Security review completed and findings triaged or mitigated; data shown in Console excludes PII and audit events follow retention policy.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Auction complexity introduces instability in control plane. Mitigation: Start with conservative defaults, single-region pilot, and circuit-breaker to disable auctions if error rate increases >2x.
Risk: Tenants observe perceived unfairness. Mitigation: Provide transparent scoring explanation in Console and allow tenants to opt into ephemeral auctions or opt out.
Risk: Backfill causes cache thrashing increasing latency. Mitigation: Backfill only if kernel scheduling estimate for pre-warm < threshold and limit backfill concurrency per GPU node.
Risk: Billing disputes over credits. Mitigation: Keep initial credit model internal and free for pilot customers; surface credits as neutral telemetry until policy finalized.
open_questions: Should credits be purchased monthly or allocated as a smooth rolling budget?
What is the canonical tenant priority signal (contract tier, observed latency, customer-provided priority)?
How should auctions interact with Dedicated autoscale pre-warm triggers (should pre-warm be reserved when auction wins)?
What telemetry thresholds should trigger automatic disablement of auctions in a region?
milestones: M1 - Spec sign-off and API contract (2026-03-20)
M2 - Auction engine MVP + unit tests (2026-04-03)
M3 - Backfill integration and runtime safeguards (2026-04-17)
M4 - Console surfaces + E2E tests + staging pilot (2026-05-01)
M5 - Gradual rollout and post-launch metrics review (2026-05-15)
